js.Il se soigne, reçoit ses visiteurs et gr: He heals, welcomes his visitors and grows with the crowd, without you lifting a finger.
Kubi dances, well fed, well configured.

js.Pendant le rolling update, la readiness: During the rolling update, the readiness probe from the Self-reliant chapter protected the visitors.
js.Deux œufs, un budget, une maintenance ré: Two eggs, a budget, a successful maintenance.
js.node-1 a été entretenu sans que Kubi s’a: node-1 was serviced without Kubi stopping for a second.
js.L’HPA du chapitre Autonome a continué de: The HPA from the Self-reliant chapter kept handling the crowd during the move.
js.Plus de root, une porte fermée, un porta: No more root, a closed door, an open gateway.
js.Kubi est protégé à l’intérieur et accuei: Kubi is protected inside and welcoming outside.
js.Le Service du chapitre Autonome sert mai: The Service from the Self-reliant chapter is now the target of the Gateway.
js.Kubernetes le fait vivre, et tu sais lir: Kubernetes keeps him alive, and you know how to read his health record.
js.Kubi se soigne tout seul : figé, il redé: Kubi heals on his own: frozen, he restarts; lost, he is replaced.
js.C’est le Deployment, ta promesse du débu: It is the Deployment, your promise from the start, that hatches the replacements.
js.Une porte, un réveil, une couleur, une c: A door, a wake-up call, a colour, a key.
js.Les visiteurs ne vont que chez les Kubi: Visitors only go to Kubis that are awake, and his config lives outside the image.
js.Les clones du chapitre Santé se partagen: The clones from the Health chapter now share the visits.

js.La readiness probe évite d’envoyer des v: The readiness probe avoids sending visitors to a v2 Kubi that is not awake yet.
A plate and a table booking.
js.Plus d’indigestion, et le scheduler sait: No more indigestion, and the scheduler knows where to put each Kubi.
js.Deux œufs, un déménagement, une foule et: Two eggs, a move, a crowd and a backup.
js.La maison encaisse maintenances, foules: The house withstands maintenance, crowds and outages.
js.Les requests du chapitre Santé guident l: The requests from the Health chapter guide the scheduler when the Kubis move.
js.Kubi et Kubo partagent la maison sans se: Kubi and Kubo share the house without stepping on each other.
js.Ce sont les mêmes œufs qu’avant, mais ch: Same eggs as before, but everyone keeps their own things.
js.Kubi reçoit des visiteurs de l’extérieur: Kubi welcomes visitors from outside, on kubi.local.
js.Une maintenance ne fait jamais tomber Ku: A maintenance never drops Kubi below 2 ready pods.
js.Pendant ce temps, le portail Gateway con: Meanwhile, the Gateway keeps welcoming visitors.
js.Plus de clés root, des portes fermées, u: No more root keys, closed doors, a badge for Kubo.
js.Même piraté, Kubi n’aurait presque aucun: Even hacked, Kubi would have almost no power.
js.La NetworkPolicy ne laisse passer que le: The NetworkPolicy only lets the Gateway through.
js.Ce que tu as fait à la main vit maintena: What you did by hand now lives in a file.
js.Le badge et le securityContext du chapit: The badge and the securityContext from the Security chapter will have to join this logbook too.
js.Terraform construit cluster-b, Argo CD y: Terraform builds cluster-b, Argo CD installs Kubi there.
js.Chacun son métier : Terraform pour la ma: Each to their own job: Terraform for the house, Git and Argo CD for its residents.
js.Argo CD lit le carnet kubi.yaml, version: Argo CD reads the kubi.yaml logbook, versioned in Git.
js.L’œuf attend que tu le fasses éclore. Re: The egg is waiting for you to hatch it. Read the info card, then type help.
js.Un Kubi est mal en point, ou une version: A Kubi is unwell, or a version is crashing. Look with kubectl get pods.
js.kubectl describe pod <pod> et kubectl lo: kubectl describe pod <pod> and kubectl logs <pod>. Frozen pod: kubectl delete pod <pod>. Broken version: kubectl rollout undo deployment/kubi
js.Pas de mode d’emploi cette fois. Kubi do: No instructions this time. Kubi must be able to live without you: it is up to you to find out how. His needs tick themselves off. Stuck? Ask for a hint.
js.Un seul Kubi, c’est fragile : s’il tombe: A single Kubi is fragile: if he falls, nobody is left. What if he had clones?
js.Se soigner tout seul quand il se fige: Heal on his own when he freezes
js.Qui vérifie que Kubi répond encore ? Jet: Who checks that Kubi still answers? Take a look at the files with ls.
js.cat kubi-liveness-probe.yaml, puis kubec: cat kubi-liveness-probe.yaml, then kubectl apply -f kubi-liveness-probe.yaml
js.Les visiteurs frappent, mais il n’y a pa: Visitors are knocking, but there is no fixed door.
js.N’accueillir personne avant d’être révei: Let nobody in before waking up
js.Un Kubi qui vient d’éclore n’est pas prê: A Kubi that just hatched is not ready right away. There is one more file to look at.
js.Qui ajoute des Kubi quand la foule arriv: Who adds Kubis when the crowd arrives? Careful, it counts as a percentage of reserved CPU.
js.kubectl set resources deployment kubi --: kubectl set resources deployment kubi --requests=cpu=100m, then kubectl autoscale deployment kubi --min=3 --max=5 --cpu-percent=50
js.Kubi veut apprendre à danser, et il a qu: Kubi wants to learn to dance, and he has a few health issues to sort out along the way. The pantry has just opened too: a new Kubi without a password will not start. Only v1 is known to be stable: it is up to you to check the others.
js.Les nouvelles images font danser Kubi. E: The new images make Kubi dance. Try one, and watch whether it holds up with real visitors.
js.kubi:v2 plante en prod. Si tu l’as essay: kubi:v2 crashes in prod. If you tried it: kubectl rollout undo deployment/kubi. The good one: kubectl set image deployment/kubi kubi=kubi:v3
js.Des Kubi sont tués en OOMKilled : leur a: Kubis are killed with OOMKilled: their plate, the memory limit, is too small.
js.Sa couleur vient d’une ConfigMap: His colour comes from a ConfigMap
js.La couleur ne doit pas vivre dans l’imag: The colour must not live in the image. Put it in a config, then wake the Kubis up.
js.kubectl create configmap kubi-config --f: kubectl create configmap kubi-config --from-literal=color=purple, then kubectl rollout restart deployment/kubi
js.Son mot de passe vient d’un Secret: His password comes from a Secret
js.Le garde-manger a un mot de passe. On ne: The pantry has a password. Never paste it into the image.
js.kubectl create secret generic kubi-secre: kubectl create secret generic kubi-secret --from-literal=password=miam, then kubectl set env deployment/kubi --from=secret/kubi-secret
js.Un deuxième œuf, node-2, vient d’arriver: A second egg, node-2, has just arrived. And node-1 is due for maintenance soon. Kubi must never stop.
All the Kubis sleep in the same egg. If node-1 falls, everyone falls. A file can spread them out (ls).
js.Une maintenance ne descend jamais sous 2: A maintenance never drops below 2 Kubis
js.Pendant une maintenance, combien de Kubi: During a maintenance, how many Kubis must stay standing? There is a budget for that.
js.node-1 doit être vidé proprement avant l: node-1 must be emptied cleanly before servicing, then reopened.
js.kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets: kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets, then kubectl uncordon node-1
js.Kubo, le petit cousin, emménage. Il est: Kubo, the little cousin, is moving in. Time to put on some locks and open a real entrance to the world.
js.Kubi ne tourne plus en root: Kubi no longer runs as root
js.Demande à Kubi qui il est : kubectl exec: Ask Kubi who he is: kubectl exec <pod> -- id. A file takes away his keys.
js.Kubo doit tourner dans chaque œuf, et vi: Kubo must run in every egg, and live in his own room. It is not a Deployment (ls).
js.kubectl create namespace nursery, cat ku: kubectl create namespace nursery, cat kubo-daemonset.yaml, then kubectl apply -f kubo-daemonset.yaml
js.Kubo ne peut plus entrer chez Kubi: Kubo can no longer get into Kubi’s place
js.Vérifie d’abord : Kubo joint-il Kubi ? k: Check first: can Kubo reach Kubi? kubectl exec -n nursery <kubo> -- curl kubi.default. Then close the door.
js.kubectl apply -f kubi-netpol.yaml, puis: kubectl apply -f kubi-netpol.yaml, then run the curl again
js.Le Service kubi ne s’ouvre qu’au cluster: The kubi Service only opens to the cluster. You need a gateway to the world (ls).
js.cat kubi-gateway.yaml, puis kubectl appl: cat kubi-gateway.yaml, then kubectl apply -f kubi-gateway.yaml
js.Kubi, c’est ton application, par exemple: Kubi is your application, for example your company’s online shop. The Deployment tells Kubernetes: run this version of my app, and keep it alive.
js.Quand un client dit « le site rame », c’: When a customer says “the site is slow”, this is where the investigation starts: get for the state, describe for the details, events for the history.
js.Ton appli tourne, mais ne répond plus :: Your app is running, but no longer answers: the process is alive, customers see a blank page. Deleting the pod is Kubernetes’ “turn it off and on again”.
js.Plusieurs copies de ta boutique tournent: Several copies of your shop run at the same time. If one falls, customers are served by the others without noticing anything.
js.Un health check automatique : Kubernetes: An automatic health check: Kubernetes polls your app every 5 s and restarts it if it stops answering, even at 3 a.m.
js.Une fuite mémoire ou un gros pic : ton a: A memory leak or a big spike: your app goes over its allowed RAM and the system kills it. Limits stop a greedy app from starving its neighbours on the same server.
js.Les requests, c’est ce que ton appli rés: Requests are what your app reserves on a server. The scheduler uses them to decide where to place it, like booking a room.
js.Une adresse fixe pour joindre ton appli,: A fixed address to reach your app, whatever the number of copies or their restarts. The other services in your system go through it.
js.Ton appli met quelques secondes à démarr: Your app takes a few seconds to start: cache, database connection… Readiness avoids sending customers to a copy that is not ready yet.
js.La configuration de ton appli : URL d’un: Your app’s configuration: an API URL, a theme, enabled options. It changes per environment (test, prod) without rebuilding the app.
js.Le mot de passe de ta base de données, o: Your database password, or an API key. Never in the code or the image: in a Secret, injected at startup.
js.Le point d’entrée public de ton système: The public entry point of your system: it receives traffic for shop.example.com and sends it to the right service. Just one for all your apps.
js.Tu livres une nouvelle fonctionnalité. L: You ship a new feature. The rolling update replaces the copies one by one: your customers never see any downtime.
js.La nouvelle version plante en production: The new version crashes in production on a Friday night. Rollback puts back the previous version in one command; you'll hunt the bug on Monday.
js.L’historique des livraisons : quelle ver: The release history: which version was running, and which one to go back to if things go wrong.
js.Le correctif est prêt : on relivre la fo: The fix is ready: you ship the feature again, this time without the bug.
js.Tes copies tournent sur des serveurs dif: Your copies run on different servers. If one server dies, the shop stays online.
js.Une règle pour l’équipe infra : pendant: A rule for the infra team: during maintenance, at least 2 copies of your app keep running.
js.La mise à jour d’un serveur (sécurité, s: Updating a server (security, OS). You empty it cleanly, update it, and put it back in service, without customers noticing a thing.
js.Les soldes, le Black Friday, un passage: Sales, Black Friday, a TV mention: traffic explodes. The autoscaler adds copies when things heat up, and removes them afterwards so you don't pay for nothing.
js.La sauvegarde de la configuration de tou: The backup of the whole cluster's configuration. Without it, a control plane crash means redeploying everything by hand.
js.Un agent de supervision ou de logs (node: A monitoring or logging agent (node-exporter, Fluent Bit, the Datadog agent) must run on every server: that's a DaemonSet. It belongs to another team, so it lives in its own namespace.
js.« Mon appli a disparu ! » Non : tu regar: “My app disappeared!” No: you were just looking in the wrong namespace.
js.Si un pirate exploite une faille de ton: If an attacker exploits a flaw in your app, they get its rights. As root, they'd have the keys to the whole container.
js.Par défaut, n’importe quelle appli du cl: By default, any app in the cluster can call yours. You close everything, and only open to those who need it.
js.Un outil de supervision doit lire l’état: A monitoring tool needs to read pod status, not passwords. You give it exactly the rights it needs, nothing more.
js.Tout ton déploiement décrit dans des fic: Your whole deployment described in files versioned in Git: reviewed in a Pull Request, reproducible, and reversible with a revert.
js.Ton plan de reprise d’activité : si le c: Your disaster recovery plan: if the main cluster goes down, a second identical environment takes over.
js.Ton appli doit tenir seule en production: Your app has to run on its own in production: get back up after a failure, serve its customers, absorb the peaks.
js.Une vraie livraison : nouvelle version,: A real release: new version, memory settings, configuration and the database password.
js.L’infra bouge sous ton appli : nouveaux: The infra moves under your app: new servers, maintenance. Your customers must not notice anything.
js.Avant d’ouvrir au public : sécurité, iso: Before opening to the public: security, isolation between teams, and a real entry point.
js.Kubi est né, et Kubernetes veille sur lu: Kubi is born, and Kubernetes watches over him.
An egg, an image, and the will to live. The Deployment is your promise to Kubernetes: “I want a Kubi running”. Kubernetes handles the rest and watches over him.
You can read Kubi's health record.
js.Avant de soigner un animal, on l’observe: Before caring for a pet, you watch it. get pods: who's there? describe: its health record. events: the cluster's logbook. It's your first reflex when something's off.
js.kubectl get pods, kubectl describe pod <: kubectl get pods, kubectl describe pod <pod>, then kubectl get events
js.Un neuf l’a remplacé tout de suite : un: A new one replaced it right away: a pod is replaceable.
js.Un Kubi peut rester Running… et ne plus: A Kubi can stay Running… and stop answering entirely. Don't panic: delete that pod. The Deployment hatches a new one right away.
js.kubectl logs <pod>, puis kubectl delete: kubectl logs <pod>, then kubectl delete pod <pod>
One Kubi falling no longer takes anything down.
js.Un seul Kubi, c’est fragile : s’il tombe: A single Kubi is fragile: if he falls, nobody's left. With 3 replicas, three identical Kubis take turns. One falls? The other two keep the shop running.
js.Kubi se fait redémarrer tout seul quand: Kubi gets restarted automatically when he freezes.
js.La liveness probe, c’est un petit « tu e: The liveness probe is a little “are you alive?” every 5 seconds. No answer? The kubelet restarts his container, without you lifting a finger.
js.Plus d’indigestion : Kubi a la place de: No more indigestion: Kubi has room to finish his meal.
js.Kubi mange plus que sa limite mémoire ?: Kubi eats more than his memory limit? He's cut off on the spot: OOMKilled. Limits set the maximum size of his plate. Give him enough room to finish his meal.
js.kubectl describe pod <pod>, puis kubectl: kubectl describe pod <pod>, then kubectl set resources deployment kubi --limits=memory=256Mi
js.Le scheduler sait où installer chaque Ku: The scheduler knows where to seat each Kubi. Asking too much leaves him Pending.
js.Les requests, c’est la réservation au re: Requests are a restaurant booking: the scheduler only seats Kubi where a table is free. Here, each egg has 1Gi. Book too big and Kubi waits outside, Pending, while the old ones keep serving.
js.kubectl set resources deployment kubi --: kubectl set resources deployment kubi --requests=memory=2Gi --limits=memory=2Gi (look at the Pending pod), kubectl describe pod <Pending pod>, then kubectl set resources deployment kubi --requests=memory=200Mi --limits=memory=256Mi
js.Une porte fixe, et les visites réparties: A fixed door, and visits spread across the Kubis.
js.Les visiteurs veulent jouer, mais un pod: Visitors want to play, but a pod changes address every time it's reborn. The Service gives them a fixed door and spreads the visits across the pods. The pods behind the door are the endpoints.
js.kubectl expose deployment kubi --port=80: kubectl expose deployment kubi --port=80, then kubectl get endpoints kubi
js.Les visiteurs n’arrivent que chez les Ku: Visitors only reach Kubis that are awake.
js.Un Kubi qui vient d’éclore a besoin de q: A freshly hatched Kubi needs a few seconds. The readiness probe asks him “are you ready?”. As long as he says no, he stays alive, but the Service sends him nothing.
js.cat kubi-readiness-probe.yaml, puis kube: cat kubi-readiness-probe.yaml, then kubectl apply -f kubi-readiness-probe.yaml
js.La couleur vit hors de l’image : on la c: The color lives outside the image: you change it without rebuilding anything.
js.Kubi rêve de violet. Plutôt que de refai: Kubi dreams of purple. Rather than rebuilding the image, put his color in a ConfigMap. He reads it when he wakes up: a rollout restart, and the new Kubis change color.
js.Le mot de passe arrive en variable d’env: The password arrives as an environment variable, never in the image.
js.Le garde-manger de Kubi vient d’ouvrir,: Kubi's pantry just opened, with a password. From now on, a new Kubi without the password crashes on startup. You don't paste that password into the image: you store it in a Secret. Careful, it's base64, not a safe.
js.kubectl create secret generic kubi-secre: kubectl create secret generic kubi-secret --from-literal=password=miam, kubectl get secret kubi-secret -o yaml, then kubectl set env deployment/kubi --from=secret/kubi-secret
js.Le Service kubi est de type ClusterIP :: The kubi Service is of type ClusterIP: only pods in the cluster can reach it. A LoadBalancer Service would open Kubi to the world, but with one entrance (and one bill) per app. The Gateway is one big door for the whole house: it welcomes visitors, and the HTTPRoute guides those for kubi.local to the right Service.
js.cat kubi-gateway.yaml, kubectl apply -f: cat kubi-gateway.yaml, kubectl apply -f kubi-gateway.yaml, kubectl get gateway, then kubectl get httproute
v2 arrives without cutting anyone off.
js.Nouvelle version, nouveau talent : en v2: New version, new talent: in v2, Kubi dances with his visitors ♪. The rolling update replaces the Kubis one by one. Watch the screen: both versions live side by side, and visitors go from ♥ (v1) to ♪ (v2) without a break.
js.kubectl set image deployment/kubi kubi=k: kubectl set image deployment/kubi kubi=kubi:v2, then kubectl rollout status deployment/kubi
js.Retour à la v1 stable en une commande. L: Back to the stable v1 in one command. The dancing will wait.
js.La v2 avait passé le rollout… puis plant: v2 passed the rollout… then crashes with real visitors. rollout undo puts back the previous version in one command. Fix first, investigate later.
js.kubectl get pods, kubectl logs <pod>, pu: kubectl get pods, kubectl logs <pod>, then kubectl rollout undo deployment/kubi
You know which revision to go back to.
js.Chaque changement du template de pod cré: Every change to the pod template creates a revision. The history shows what you can go back to.
js.Même geste qu’avec la v2. Cette fois, le: Same move as with v2. This time, the new pods become ready and replace the old ones.
js.Les Kubi sont étalés : un œuf qui tombe: The Kubis are spread out: one falling egg doesn't take everyone down.
js.Ne mets pas tous tes Kubi dans le même œ: Don't put all your Kubis in one egg
js.Un deuxième œuf, node-2, vient d’être br: A second egg, node-2, was just plugged in. But all the Kubis stayed in the first one: if node-1 falls, everyone falls. topologySpreadConstraints makes the scheduler spread them out.
js.kubectl get pods -o wide, cat kubi-sprea: kubectl get pods -o wide, cat kubi-spread.yaml, then kubectl apply -f kubi-spread.yaml
js.Une maintenance ne laisse jamais Kubi so: Maintenance never leaves Kubi under 2 ready pods.
js.Pendant une maintenance, on fait déménag: During maintenance, the Kubis move out. The PodDisruptionBudget sets the rule: at least 2 Kubis ready at all times. drain respects it and moves the pods one by one.
js.kubectl create pdb kubi --selector=app=k: kubectl create pdb kubi --selector=app=kubi --min-available=2, then kubectl get pdb
js.drain, puis uncordon ou delete node: drain, then uncordon or delete node
node-1 is emptied without cutting Kubi off.
js.node-1 part en maintenance. drain le fer: node-1 goes into maintenance. drain closes it to newcomers (cordon), then moves its pods to node-2. Thanks to the replicas, Kubi never stops. Then: uncordon to reopen the egg, or delete node to remove it.
js.kubectl get pods -o wide, kubectl drain: kubectl get pods -o wide, kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets, then kubectl uncordon node-1 (maintenance done) or kubectl delete node node-1 (node removed)
js.Un œuf fermé ne bloque plus le déménagem: A closed egg no longer blocks the move.
js.Pourquoi un Kubi reste dehors ?: Why is a Kubi left outside?
js.Pendant le déménagement, un Kubi est res: During the move, a Kubi stayed Pending. The culprit: the spread. Cordoned node-1 still counts in the math with 0 Kubis, so node-2 can't get more than one ahead (maxSkew: 1). nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor tells the scheduler to ignore closed eggs.
js.kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets: kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets, kubectl get pods, kubectl describe pod <Pending pod>, cat kubi-spread-fix.yaml, kubectl apply -f kubi-spread-fix.yaml, kubectl get pods, then kubectl uncordon node-1
js.HPA de 2 à 5 replicas, request CPU: HPA from 2 to 5 replicas, CPU request
js.Kubi grandit pendant la foule et rétréci: Kubi grows during the crowd and shrinks afterwards.
js.Les jours de foule, 3 Kubi ne suffisent: On crowd days, 3 Kubis aren't enough. The HorizontalPodAutoscaler adds more when the CPU heats up. It thinks in percentages: “Kubi uses 80% of what he reserved”. If Kubi reserved nothing (no CPU request), 80% of nothing means nothing: the HPA shows <unknown> and does nothing.
js.kubectl autoscale deployment kubi --min=: kubectl autoscale deployment kubi --min=2 --max=5 --cpu-percent=50, kubectl get hpa (the TARGETS column shows cpu: <unknown>), kubectl describe hpa kubi (missing request for cpu), kubectl set resources deployment kubi --requests=cpu=100m,memory=200Mi --limits=memory=256Mi (Kubi reserves 0.1 CPU), then kubectl get hpa (a real percentage appears) and wait for the crowd
The droppings disappear on their own.
js.Les crottes (pods évincés) s’accumulent: Droppings (evicted pods) pile up in the eggs. Cleaning is the job of kube-controller-manager's pod GC… which waits for 12,500 droppings by default! It's a static pod: edit its manifest, and the kubelet restarts it on its own.
js.kubectl get pods -n kube-system, cat /et: kubectl get pods -n kube-system, cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml, then sed -i "s/--terminated-pod-gc-threshold=12500/--terminated-pod-gc-threshold=1/" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml (the trash button prepares the command)
js.etcd, c’est la mémoire du cluster : tout: etcd is the cluster's memory: everything is written there. If the control plane dies without a backup, everything is forgotten. Take a snapshot, then check it's readable.
js.ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /bac: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /backup/etcd.db, then etcdutl snapshot status /backup/etcd.db
js.Un Kubo dans chaque œuf, dans sa propre: One Kubo in every egg, in his own room.
js.Kubo, le petit cousin de Kubi, devient l: Kubo, Kubi's little cousin, becomes the house's guardian: he has to be in every egg to watch over it. A Deployment doesn't guarantee that, a DaemonSet does: exactly one Kubo per egg, even in eggs that arrive later. And he gets his own room, a namespace.
js.kubectl create namespace nursery, cat ku: kubectl create namespace nursery, cat kubo-daemonset.yaml, kubectl apply -f kubo-daemonset.yaml, then kubectl get daemonset -n nursery
You know which room to look in.
js.Tu tapes kubectl get pods… et pas de Kub: You type kubectl get pods… and no Kubo! Without -n, kubectl only looks in the default room. -n opens another room, -A walks around the whole house.
js.kubectl get pods (Kubo n’y est pas), kub: kubectl get pods (Kubo isn't there), kubectl get pods -n nursery, then kubectl get pods -A
js.Kubi mange une image sans faille connue,: Kubi eats an image with no known flaw, and always exactly the same one.
js.Une image, c’est la nourriture de Kubi :: An image is Kubi's food: you need to know what's in it. Trivy scans kubi:v3 and finds a flaw. v3.1 is fixed. You deploy it by its digest: a tag can be rewritten, a digest always points to exactly the same image.
js.trivy image kubi:v3, trivy image kubi:v3: trivy image kubi:v3, trivy image kubi:v3.1, then kubectl set image deployment/kubi kubi=kubi@sha256:<digest> (the syringe button prepares the command)
js.Un Kubi piraté n’a plus les clés de la m: A hacked Kubi no longer has the house keys.
js.Par défaut, Kubi tourne en root : il a l: By default, Kubi runs as root: he has the keys to the whole house, and an attacker who takes him over would have them too. The securityContext gives him a simple badge: non-root user, read-only files.
js.kubectl exec <pod> -- id, cat kubi-secur: kubectl exec <pod> -- id, cat kubi-secure.yaml, kubectl apply -f kubi-secure.yaml, then kubectl exec <new pod> -- id
js.Seule la Gateway entre chez Kubi. Kubo r: Only the Gateway gets into Kubi's room. Kubo stays in his.
js.Par défaut, toutes les chambres communiq: By default, all rooms are connected: Kubo walks into Kubi's without knocking. A NetworkPolicy closes the doors and only lets the Gateway in. You need a CNI that enforces it, like Calico or Cilium.

js.Tout ce que tu as tapé à la main, tu fin: Everything you typed by hand, you'll end up forgetting. Write it in kubi.yaml and keep it in Git. diff shows what changed, apply brings the cluster back in line with the notebook. That's the basis of GitOps.
